ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two operational amplifier stages, the left side is IC1A, and the right side is IC1B. The output terminal is labeled Vo, located on the right side, and connected to the output node of IC1B. The feedback resistor R5 is labeled 50 kΩ and is drawn above the circuit; one end of it is connected to the right-side output node Vo, and the other end is connected back to a node on the left side; this node is simultaneously connected through R1 to ground, and is connected into the non-inverting input terminal “+” of IC1A. Reasoning: R5 samples from the output terminal Vo, therefore the sampled object is the output voltage, belonging to voltage feedback; R5 returns to the path of the non-inverting input terminal of IC1A, therefore the feedback signal and the input are mixed at the input terminal in a series manner, and can be classified as series feedback; because the feedback is sent to the non-inverting “+” terminal, when the output increases it will make the potential of the non-inverting terminal increase in the same direction, and the feedback polarity is positive feedback. Therefore what R5 introduces is voltage series positive feedback.

raw_record.question_text: What type of feedback is introduced by the feedback resistor \(R_5\) in the operational-amplifier circuit shown in the figure?

method.method_draft: First inspect the figure and trace R5 from the output node Vo back to the node at IC1A’s + input. Since R5 samples the output voltage and returns it to the non-inverting input path, classify the sampling as voltage feedback, the input mixing as series feedback, and the sign as positive. Therefore the feedback introduced by R5 is voltage-series positive feedback.
